frontmatter.title: Model Loading

blocks.content: Aspose.3D enables loading 3D models in TypeScript environments, supporting common formats for use in 3d typescript game engines and 3d typescript applications. This page covers model loading workflows for developers integrating 3d typescript libraries into production-grade 3d game or visualization projects.

The `Scene` class provides the primary entry point for loading 3D scenes from files or streams. Developers can load models from local paths or remote URLs, then inspect or manipulate the resulting scene graph using the core types exposed by the Aspose.3D package.

Aspose.3D provides foundational support for loading and inspecting 3D model data in TypeScript environments. Developers can work with core 3D entities such as scenes, nodes, and geometries using the `Scene`, `Node`, and `Geometry` classes from the Aspose.3D package. This section outlines essential data operations—reading, writing, and modifying elements—within a 3D model workflow.

To inspect a 3D model, load it into a `Scene` object and traverse its node hierarchy. Accessing vertex data, materials, or transforms requires navigating through `Node` and `Geometry` instances. The API supports reading mesh topology and material assignments, enabling validation or preprocessing before rendering or export.

Modify node transforms, geometry properties, or material assignments by directly updating object fields after loading. Changes to vertex positions, normals, or UV coordinates are applied in-memory and can be verified before persisting. The `Node` and `Geometry` classes expose mutable properties for common mesh attributes.

Persist modified or newly constructed 3D scenes to disk using the `save()` method on `Scene`. Supported formats include FBX, OBJ, and glTF. The save operation serializes the full node tree, geometry, and material state into the target format.

Aspose.3D enables loading 3D models in TypeScript environments, supporting common workflows for 3D typescript game engines and 3D typescript applications. Developers can load model files using the core `Scene` class, which serves as the entry point for parsing and representing 3D scenes in memory. This section provides runnable examples demonstrating how to load a 3D model file and inspect its contents using only the documented API surface.

When loading 3D models in a TypeScript environment using Aspose.3D, memory usage and performance depend heavily on file size and format complexity. Large models may cause high memory consumption or delays during parsing, especially when loading from remote sources or in real-time applications like 3D game engines. Always dispose of `Scene` instances after use to release native resources, and prefer streaming or chunked loading for large assets where supported by the underlying format.

items: Use `Scene` only for the duration needed and call its `dispose()` method to prevent memory leaks in long-running applications.
Prefer binary formats like FBX or glTF over text-based formats for faster parsing and smaller memory footprints.
Avoid loading the same model multiple times; cache `Scene` instances when reusing assets across scenes or frames.
Monitor stack depth and recursion limits when loading deeply nested scenes, as some formats may trigger deep call stacks during deserialization.
